about: Example Western ECI dictionary entries and whether each is valid. Each example gives an ECI voice code, a slot (main, root or abbr, as in the <voice><slot>.dic filename), a key, a value, and the expected result: "valid", or the identifier of the one rule the entry breaks. Identifiers are explained under "reasons". Format and usage: docs/research/eci-dic-format.md, section 11.

reasons.keyTab: The key contains a tab, which is the key/value separator.
reasons.valueTab: The value contains a tab, which is the key/value separator.
reasons.keyNewline: The key contains a carriage return or line feed.
reasons.valueNewline: The value contains a carriage return or line feed.
reasons.keyNul: The key contains a NUL character, which truncates the engine's C string.
reasons.valueNul: The value contains a NUL character, which truncates the engine's C string.
reasons.mainKeyFinalPunctuation: A main key ends with a punctuation character.
reasons.rootKeyInvalid: A root key is not letters with optional internal apostrophes. An apostrophe may not be first, last, or next to another apostrophe.
reasons.rootValueInvalid: A root value is not one word of letters or one bare SPR (`[...]).
reasons.abbreviationKeyInvalid: An abbreviation key is not letters separated by single periods, with an optional trailing period and optional internal apostrophes. Hyphens and other punctuation are invalid.
reasons.abbreviationValueInvalid: An abbreviation value is not words of letters separated by single spaces or hyphens.
reasons.unencodableCharacter: The key or value contains a character the voice's code page cannot encode. All Western voices use Windows-1252.
reasons.sprUnclosed: An SPR opened with `[ has no closing ] before the next `[ or the end of the value.
reasons.sprEmpty: An SPR has nothing between `[ and ].
reasons.sprQuoteInvalid: An SPR has an unmatched apostrophe, or a quoted symbol that is not exactly two characters.
reasons.sprPrimaryStressRequired: An SPR with more than one syllable has no primary stress marker 1.

examples.note: Mechanical rules apply in every slot.
Main keys are case-sensitive; this does not change lowercase who.

examples.value: jeb at not real dot org
examples.note: Internal punctuation is allowed in main keys.
Annotations are allowed in main values.
A final apostrophe counts as punctuation.
Root keys are case-insensitive; EDM stores them in lowercase.
Internal apostrophes are valid in root keys, although the ECI manual says letters only. The bundled enuroot.dic has 112 such keys.
Accented letters that Windows-1252 can encode are letters.
Annotations are not allowed in root values.
An SPR must be the whole root value.
Apostrophes are allowed in root keys, not root values.
A trailing period means the key matches only Dr. with the period.
Without a trailing period the key matches approx with or without a following period.
Hyphens are invalid in abbreviation keys. Use a main entry instead.
SPRs are not allowed in abbreviation values.
The euro sign is in Windows-1252 but not ISO-8859-1.
Letters outside Windows-1252 fail the encoding rule, not the root key rule.
Two-character symbols are quoted with apostrophes. One syllable needs no stress marker.
SPR structure is checked in root values too.
Phoneme symbols are not checked against the voice's symbol table.
